questions.question: List the four steps for locating a place in the news on a map.
questions.expected_answer: Find the place name in the news story. Look it up in the atlas index to find the page and grid reference or degrees. Read or check its latitude and longitude with directions. Mark it on the map with a pin or dot and label it with the date, the place, its position and a short headline.

questions.question: Name two real news events and give the approximate position of each place in degrees.
questions.expected_answer: The April 2022 floods in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, at about thirty degrees south, thirty-one degrees east. Cyclone Idai near Beira in Mozambique in March 2019, at about twenty degrees south, thirty-five degrees east. Other answers could include the 2023 earthquake in Morocco at about thirty-one degrees north, eight degrees west, or the 2023 Rugby World Cup final in Paris at about forty-nine degrees north, two degrees east.

questions.question: Why should a geographer ask why an event happened where it did? Give an example.
questions.expected_answer: Asking why helps us understand the link between places and events, and helps people prepare. For example, Cyclone Idai caused floods around Beira because cyclones form over warm oceans and the coastal land there is low and flat, so water from the sea and heavy rain spread over it easily.
